title: No Fare
plain_title: Fare and toll evasion cost the MTA about $1 billion in 2024
what_they_audited: A Citizens Budget Commission report estimating the revenue the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) loses to fare and toll evasion and reviewing its enforcement and other responses.
background: In May 2023 the MTA's Blue-Ribbon Panel on Fare Evasion recommended a four-pronged approach of enforcement, environment, education and equity.

findings.plain: Unpaid fares and tolls cost the transit agency roughly $1 billion in 2024.
findings.quote: Fare and toll evasion cost the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) approximately $1 billion in revenue in 2024.

findings.plain: Buses accounted for the largest share of the loss, followed by subways, commuter rail and tolls.
findings.quote: $568 million in unpaid bus fares, $350 million in unpaid subway fares, at least $46 million in unpaid commuter rail tickets, and at least $51 million in unpaid tolls

findings.plain: The subway evasion rate fell over the year to the first quarter of 2025.
findings.quote: Between the first quarter of 2024 and the first quarter of 2025, the subway fare evasion rate declined from 14 percent to 10 percent

findings.plain: Bus evasion also declined but stayed far higher than subway evasion.
findings.quote: The bus fare evasion rate declined from 48 percent to 44 percent during that period.

findings.plain: Civil summonses rose sharply after 2021 before falling back in early 2025, while arrests, though much rarer, increased.
findings.quote: The number of civil summonses increased from 13,607 in the third quarter of 2021 to a peak of 38,422 in the third quarter of 2024, before declining to 29,046 in the first quarter of 2025

findings.plain: The scale of evasion in 2024 amounted to hundreds of unpaid rides every minute.
findings.quote: every minute during 2024, 330 subway fares and 710 bus fares were evaded

findings.plain: If the recent trend holds, losses in 2025 would be lower but still large.

recommendations: Refine and continue a multi-faceted approach to reducing fare and toll evasion covering enforcement, rider education and securing the system environment, and publish data showing how cost-effective each intervention is.
Speed up the rollout of the new faregates funded in the 2025 to 2029 Capital Plan.
Speed up the rollout of proof-of-payment so EAGLE Team inspectors can enforce fare payment on local and express buses without witnessing the evasion directly.
Publish comprehensive and regular data on fare and toll evasion, including targets, quarterly evasion and lost revenue reports, quarterly unpaid toll reports and quarterly commuter rail fare reports.
Work with the city to assess how cost-effective it is to deploy police officers to enforce fare payment.
Work with the city to assess the effectiveness of Fair Fares NYC and consider expanding it, including studying the need for fare subsidies by income band and ridership.
